hardware_dossier.transmitter: 3-watt homebrew SSB transceiver built inside a biscuit tin. If a ham goes out-of-band and plays rock music, we call it a pirate; when XE9-PED goes out-of-band on 6,969.5 USB to read official methane-frost and sublimation forecasts for independent ice-harvesters, that makes him a Pirate Utility.
hardware_dossier.feedline_anomaly: Remarkable 3,700 AU reach on just 3 watts thanks to forward-scatter off ionized cometary tails.

characters.name: Capt. Rafael 'Rafa' Rodríguez
characters.role: Skipper of Ice-Tender MV Boca del Río & 'Pirate Utility' Broadcaster
characters.dialect_notes: Warm, folksy, coastal Mexican cadence mixed with cryo-barometric terminology and acoustic guitar chords.

voice_profile.cadence: 140 WPM relaxed wheelhouse delivery with nylon-string guitar harmonic intro
voice_profile.dsp_chain: 3-Watt QRP SSB biscuit-tin exciter + cometary ion-tail forward-scatter flutter

characters.signature_quote: Buenas madrugadas a toda la flota hielera en el Sector Nueve... tres vatios desde mi lata de galletas danesas, ¡pero con corazón de cincuenta kilovatios!
characters.bio: When the Sector 9 Meteorology Bureau stopped broadcasting Spanish-language ice-pack warnings to save reactor power, Capt. Rafa built a 3-watt SSB transmitter inside a round blue Danish butter-cookie tin and went out-of-band on 6,969.5 kHz USB every night from 0402 to 0415 GCT.
characters.language_sample_transcript: Buenas madrugadas a toda la flota hielera del Sector Nueve! This is Captain Rafa aboard the Boca del Río on sixty-nine-sixty-nine point five. Three watts coming out of my Danish butter-cookie tin, pero con corazón de cincuenta kilovatios!
characters.phonetic_and_conlang_notes: Veracruz Maritime Spanish & Oort Ice-Fleet Spanglish ('flota hielera', 'lata de galletas danesas').

worldbuilding.habitat_and_culture: The Pedregal Ice-Shoal is worked by dozens of family-owned ice-tugs navigating dark sub-glacial seas and emerald icebergs beneath active comet tails. Capt. Rafa's wheelhouse aboard MV Boca del Río is the unofficial town square and weather bureau for the entire fleet.
worldbuilding.spectrum_gimmick_title: 3-Watt Biscuit-Tin QRP 'Pirate Utility' via Cometary Ion-Tail Scatter
worldbuilding.hauser_commentary: At 0411 on 6969.5 USB, Capt. Rafa aboard the ice-tender Boca del Río with his nightly frost forecast. If a ham goes out of band and plays rock music we call it a pirate; going out of band on 3 watts to read official ice-tug weather makes him a Pirate Utility! Proud to hold QSL #1 from his butter-cookie-tin rig.
worldbuilding.qsl_postcard_style: Homemade Wheelhouse Snapshot & Clip-Art Tower Postcard (inspired by Voice of Pancho Villa)
worldbuilding.qsl_animation_notes: 2-frame wheelhouse action: Capt. Rafa raises his hand in a big warm wave while the vacuum tube atop his blue cookie-tin transmitter flares golden-orange and the clip-art '3W BIG SIGNAL!' tower radiates!

discovery_arc.summary: Received QSL #1 confirming 3.0 Watts PEP from a Danish butter-cookie tin; millibar readings secretly track Grade-B Dilithium spot prices.
Rafa stays on the air past 0415 GCT on battery power to guide three ice-barges around a violent +22 Pa sublimation eruption.

flow_plates.caption: View from the frosted forward bridge windows of MV Boca del Río looking out over its ice-crusted steel bow and radar mast across a dark sea of glowing emerald icebergs and a cyan comet tail.
Capt. Rafa Rodríguez in his warm timber-lined wheelhouse holding his 3W blue Danish butter-cookie-tin SSB transmitter.
Capt. Rafa raising his left hand in a big warm wave while the vacuum tube atop his cookie-tin rig flares bright gold.
